title: When the Oath Burns
premise: Ada Thackeray, a royal food-taster whose body is a ledger of poisons survived, secretly keeps the accounts of the Guild of Impossible Things, which trades in doors to vanished countries, borrowed years, and names not yet earned. When Ada's own death date surfaces in a century-old prophecy, they learn the prophecy was written by their future self and that the last dragon-fire keeping the erased nation of Vael alive is guttering out. Hunted by the Crown's inquisitors and betrayed by the guildmaster who raised them, Ada must choose between loyalty to the people who made them invisible and the truth that they were always Vael's lost heir. In the end, Ada burns the ledgers, walks through the final door carrying the dragon-flame in their own chest, and lets the old country die so its people can finally live somewhere real.
about_author: Astrid Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed estate libraries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people whose jobs are too small for the worlds that need them.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Ada. At the royal banquet, Ada sips arsenic-laced wine and survives, then slips away to log the night's trade at the Guild of Impossible Things: a stolen hour, sold to a grieving widow. The beat is quiet competence masking loneliness; Ada believes invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Impossible
chapters.summary: POV Ada. We see the guild's back rooms: debts paid in memories, a door that opens onto Vael, a country erased from maps a century ago. Guildmaster Corvane teaches Ada that every impossible thing must be recorded or it unravels. Beat: wonder laced with unease.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Cataloguing a seized library, Ada finds a prophecy book from a hundred years past and reads tonight's date beside their own name and manner of death. The beat is vertigo; the invisible person has been seen all along.

chapters.title: What the Wine Knew
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Testing the prophecy against guild records, Ada discovers prior tasters died on their written dates—always of poison never served. Corvane orders the page burned. Beat: first crack of doubt in Ada's loyalty.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Invitation
chapters.summary: POV Inquisitor Hale. Hale, who suspects the guild exists but cannot prove it, summons Ada for routine questioning after the banquet. Their cat-and-mouse conversation reveals Hale keeps his own secret ledger. Beat: mutual recognition of two careful liars.

chapters.title: Doors That Remember
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Seeking answers, Ada steps through the guild's Vael door and finds a dying city lit by one guttering dragon-fire, inhabited by people who cannot leave without forgetting themselves. An old woman calls Ada by a name they've never heard. Beat: homesickness for a place they've never been.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Corvane reveals he bought Ada as an orphan specifically because prophecy named them—a taster raised as a shield against a written death. His tenderness curdles into ownership. Beat: grief; the only family was a transaction.

chapters.title: Poison Is a Language
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Studying the prophecy's cipher, Ada realizes it's written in tasters' shorthand—their own hand, aged a century. Someone has sent the book back through the guild's doors. Beat: terror becoming resolve.

chapters.title: The Widow's Hour
chapters.summary: POV Hale. Hale traces the stolen hour from chapter one and corners the widow, learning enough to raid the guild at dawn. Beat: his rigid justice begins to bend when her grief mirrors his own buried loss.

chapters.title: Raid on Ember Lane
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The inquisition storms the guild; ledgers burn, tasters scatter, and Corvane escapes with the master ledger, abandoning Ada to be captured. Beat: betrayal crystallized in smoke and ash.

chapters.title: Cells and Ciphers
chapters.summary: POV Ada, imprisoned. Interrogated by Hale, Ada bargains with partial truths and realizes Hale's superiors want the Vael door weaponized. Beat: two prisoners of different cages finding common cause.

chapters.title: The Escape That Cost a Name
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The widow repays her debt, smuggling Ada out using the stolen hour—but passage through impossible time erases one memory from Ada: their mother's face. Beat: sacrifice made tangible.

chapters.title: Heir of a Burned Map
chapters.summary: POV Ada. In Vael's ruins, the old woman confirms it: Ada is the last of Vael's royal line, hidden in another country's kitchens. The dragon-fire gutters lower. Beat: identity as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Corvane. He offers the Crown the door in exchange for pardon and the master ledger's power, revealing he has fed the dragon-fire with traded years for decades. Beat: villainy built from genuine love, which makes it worse.

chapters.title: Allies at the Threshold
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Hale defects with evidence of the Crown's plan; the scattered tasters regroup. To reopen the door fully, someone must feed the fire a life freely given. Beat: fragile fellowship forged in shared risk.

chapters.title: The Prophecy's Author
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Using the guild's deepest door, Ada meets their century-older self mid-writing, who explains the loop: the book was a warning meant to change the ending, not seal it. Beat: dread lifting into agency.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Owes
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Corvane captures the group and demands Ada sign the ledger transferring Vael's heirship to him, sparing their friends. Ada signs—then reveals a forged signature invalidates the transfer. Beat: cleverness as defiance.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: POV Ada. At the fire's heart, Corvane tries to take the flame by force; Hale holds the inquisitors off at terrible cost. The fire gutters to embers as dawn comes. Beat: climax opening—everything staked on one choice.

chapters.title: When the Oath Burns
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada takes the dying flame into their own body, burning the ledgers—every debt, every record, including the prophecy—so no one can own the impossible again. Corvane, unmade by his erased accounts, fades. Beat: catharsis through destruction.

chapters.title: A Country With No Door
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Carrying the flame, Ada leads Vael's people out before the last door closes forever—they will live scattered and remembered, no longer trapped in an erased nation. Beat: mourning transmuted into release.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Months later, Ada tastes for no crown, keeping instead a small open book where anyone may record what they've survived. Hale visits as a friend; the widow's name is entered first. Beat: quiet restoration of trust.

chapters.title: Somewhere Real
chapters.summary: POV Ada. On a hill above a city that appears on maps, Ada feels the dragon-fire steady in their chest—no longer a countdown but a hearth. The final beat: identity chosen, not assigned; visible at last, and glad of it.
